records.label: Hardship needs and evidence in the ESA source
records.scope: DMG 53140–53152 describe reduced-rate ESA(IR) hardship payments with conditions, claim and evidence requirements. Financial hardship is not LCW/LCWRA, and a WCA finding alone does not establish hardship payment entitlement.
records.text: The source separates hardship about immediate basic necessities from the work capability assessment and requires reasons and evidence for the hardship decision.

authority.label: Existing authored research concept; specialist review required

records.label: Household in the ESA(IR) source
records.scope: DMG 43001 limits this family and household exercise to ESA(IR). The source says the same exercise is not needed for ESA(Cont). A shared address, temporary separation or family label alone does not decide household membership.
records.text: The guidance describes a household through domestic life and ties between people, distinguishing sharing a dwelling from membership of the same household.

authority.label: Existing authored research concept; specialist review required

records.label: ESA(IR) household membership during absence
records.scope: DMG 43051–43053 include previous shared household and unconditional-return-intention qualifications. Fifty-two weeks is not a standalone universal cut-off or an imported Pension Credit rule; facts and the source’s exception must be considered together.
records.text: The source distinguishes temporary absence from an absence without intention to resume living together, and provides qualified duration and exceptional-circumstance provisions.

authority.label: Existing authored research concept; specialist review required

records.label: Period for assessing ESA income other than self-employment
records.scope: DMG 48030 expressly excludes self-employment. Earnings on termination and exceptional payments have further provisions. The assessment period is an evidence question, not an automatic bank-receipt or calendar calculation.
records.text: The source calls for the claim date, benefit-week start, due date, date treated as paid and payment period or stated alternative when deciding the period over which income is taken into account.

authority.label: Existing authored research concept; specialist review required

records.label: Benefit purpose in the source’s income-deprivation guidance
records.scope: DMG 51469, 51472–51473 and 51485–51486 name ESA(IR), IS and JSA(IB), but no cross-benefit equivalence is inferred. Explanations, timing and other evidence are relevant; disposal or non-receipt alone does not establish purpose.
records.text: The source requires a significant benefit purpose for deprivation of income and consideration of the facts, distinguishing income already received and an enforceable immediately repayable debt.

authority.label: Existing authored research concept; specialist review required

records.label: Due, received and treated-as-paid dates for ESA income
records.scope: DMG 48031 and 48048 require the relevant detailed rules and evidence. Their terminology does not establish a universal cash-receipt basis or a rule for self-employment.
records.text: The source distinguishes a payment’s due date from when it is actually made or received and from when it is treated as paid for benefit assessment.

authority.label: Authored research context; specialist review required

records.label: Income-related ESA prisoner applicable amount
records.scope: Frozen DMG research: listed legacy JSA(Cont), JSA(IB), IS, SPC and ESA(Cont)/ESA(IR) imprisonment guidance captured on 15 September 2026. This is an explanation of the captured text, not a determination of contemporary individual eligibility.
records.text: Captured DMG 54213 sets a nil applicable amount for the sentenced-prisoner branch; the 54214 example expressly ends entitlement when that amount becomes nil. Remand may retain allowable housing costs, otherwise nil. DMG 42581 treats the claimant as not having limited capability for work from the day after that remand entitlement ceases. DMG 54215/42582 require consideration of both ESA components where both apply. The civil/military-inclusive definition and hospital legislation qualification are retained; this is not a New Style ESA determination.

authority.label: Existing authored research concept; specialist review required

records.label: Period of free in-patient treatment in the ESA source
records.scope: DMG 54072–54074 apply only where the specified treatment conditions are met. These source-specific day-counting provisions are not generic hospital dates or an automatic entitlement reduction.
records.text: The source distinguishes admission and return days from discharge and temporary-leave days when identifying a period of free in-patient treatment.

authority.label: Existing authored research concept; specialist review required

records.label: Reassessment and conversion of legacy awards to ESA
records.scope: DMG 45300–45302 describe a process beginning in 2010 and national staging in 2011. The credits-only exclusion and other IS categories at 45306/45315 qualify scope. This historical conversion is not equated with a new claim or UC managed migration.
records.text: The source calls the process of deciding whether existing IB, SDA or disability-related IS awards qualify for conversion to ESA reassessment, with an existing award potentially including more than one benefit.

authority.label: Existing authored research concept; specialist review required

records.label: Limited capability for work in the ESA source
records.scope: DMG 42020–42021 are a capability definition, not a diagnosis or sufficient proof of entitlement. Points-based assessment, treated-as rules, exceptions, work and other basic conditions remain distinct. LCW and LCWRA are not interchangeable.
records.text: The source relates limited capability for work to a physical or mental condition and whether it is reasonable to require work, and describes this as the first capability question in the assessment process.

authority.label: Existing authored research concept; specialist review required

records.label: Limited capability for work-related activity in the ESA source
records.scope: DMG 42610–42613 contain general component wording. Chapter 44 paragraph 44631 expressly records removal of WRAC for specified claims from 3 April 2017 with savings. No automatic current WRAC payment is inferred from not having LCWRA, and no UC/New Style test is substituted.
records.text: The source requires a further determination of limited capability for work-related activity for a claimant with limited capability for work, and links LCWRA to the support component.

authority.label: Existing authored research concept; specialist review required

records.label: Negligible work in the source’s ESA guidance
records.scope: DMG 41145–41147 do not create a universal hours threshold or a blanket self-employment exemption. Material running, supervision or administration of a business is distinguished from negligible activity; facts and case law remain necessary.
records.text: The source describes a prior question of whether a very small amount of work is negligible, considering normal duties, effort and the contribution to a business.

authority.label: Existing authored research concept; specialist review required

records.label: Notional income in the ESA source
records.scope: DMG 51456–51462 distinguish actual income, possible notional bases, liable-relative payments and service-user exceptions. A missing payment does not establish notional income or fraud. Historical programme wording is not a current duration rule.
records.text: The source calls income not received but treated as held notional income and lists several potential bases, with normal assessment rules and any appropriate disregard.

authority.label: Existing authored research concept; specialist review required

records.label: Income other than earnings in the ESA source
records.scope: DMG 51000 and 51003 distinguish this chapter’s other income from earnings. Gross treatment has specified exceptions, including differing recovery provisions; no assertion is made that all income or every deduction is treated alike.
records.text: The source describes different other-income scope for ESA(IR) and ESA(Cont), identifying specified exceptions to the general absence of an effect on ESA(Cont).

authority.label: Existing authored research concept; specialist review required

records.label: Notional entitlement for ESA part-week payments
records.scope: DMG 46042 is a calculation-specific definition, not notional income or capital and not a promise of payment. Relevant-week selection and exceptional reductions remain separate.
records.text: For its part-week guidance, the source uses different meanings of notional entitlement: the ESA(Cont) personal rate or the ESA(IR) applicable amount exceeding income.

authority.label: Existing authored research concept; specialist review required

records.label: Relevant week for ESA part-week payments
records.scope: DMG 46043 points to separate definitions at 46052, 46082 and 46103. The relevant week cannot be assumed to be the current calendar week; no part-week award is calculated.
records.text: The source bases a part-week payment on notional entitlement for a relevant week that depends on whether the payment arises at the beginning, end or change of benefit week.

authority.label: Existing authored research concept; specialist review required

records.label: Partner and child income in the ESA(IR) source
records.scope: DMG 48008–48009 include under-eighteen couple and allowance qualifications. This is not the JSA/IS child-income wording and is not transferred to ESA(Cont), UC or Pension Credit.
records.text: The source generally treats the partner’s income as the claimant’s for ESA(IR), subject to specified exceptions, while excluding income paid to or in respect of a child or young person in the family.

authority.label: Existing authored research concept; specialist review required

records.label: Self-employed earnings assessment period for ESA
records.scope: DMG 50051 expressly says this period must not be confused with the ESA assessment phase. Newer, established and changed businesses have different provisions; the period is not automatically the preceding tax year or thirteen weeks.
records.text: The source uses gross receipts and paid expenses during an earnings assessment period and varies period selection for a new business or changed trading pattern.

authority.label: Existing authored research concept; specialist review required

records.label: Self-employed earner in the ESA source
records.scope: DMG 50007 and 50016 distinguish limited-company directors as office holders. The separate claimant/partner effects in ESA(Cont) and ESA(IR) remain explicit; neither a business label nor tax treatment alone determines the outcome.
records.text: The source describes self-employment as gainful employment in Great Britain outside employed-earner employment, while allowing a person to have separate employed work.

authority.label: Existing authored research concept; specialist review required

records.label: ESA support component in the source
records.scope: DMG 44631–44632 require the capability and phase conditions to be considered separately. This concept does not calculate a component or transfer its rules to UC or New Style ESA.
records.text: The source states that both ESA(Cont) and ESA(IR) can attract the support component, which is based on the claimant’s entitlement rather than a couple rate or the partner’s circumstances.

authority.label: Existing authored research concept; specialist review required

records.label: ESA third-party deductions and evidence of liability
records.scope: DMG 46131 and 46133–46138 retain claimant/partner distinctions: a partner’s or dependant’s fine is excluded by the cited note. Consent, limits, priority and the detailed scheme conditions remain unresolved; a bill alone is not an automated deduction decision.
records.text: The source describes discretion to pay deductions to third parties, requires liability for the debt and provides for evidence where liability is disputed.

authority.label: Existing authored research concept; specialist review required

records.label: Work in the source’s ESA general rule
records.scope: DMG 41121–41124 and 41132 separate claimant work, partner work and ESA(Cont)/ESA(IR). Unpaid activity is not automatically ignored, and all activity is not automatically disqualifying: exempt and negligible work need separate consideration.
records.text: For this ESA rule, work can be undertaken with or without expected payment. The source explicitly distinguishes that meaning from remunerative work and qualifies its general exclusion by exceptions.

authority.label: Existing authored research concept; specialist review required

records.label: ESA work-related activity and its work boundary
records.scope: DMG 53071–53077 do not authorise requiring employment, a job application or medical treatment. Requirement scope, reasonableness, exemptions, support-group status and later legal changes must be checked; no sanction decision follows from this concept.
records.text: The source distinguishes work-related activity from ordinary paid or unpaid work, differentiates a required work placement from voluntary work experience, and restricts what may be required.

authority.label: Existing authored research concept; specialist review required

records.label: The source’s 3 April 2017 WRAC boundary
records.scope: The note to DMG 44631 qualifies the general component language in chapter 42, including 42613. The date is a source-stated claims boundary, not a document publication date. Appendix 6, later amendments and personal applicability remain unresolved.
records.text: Chapter 44 records that the work-related activity component is not included for claims made on or after 3 April 2017, subject to the savings identified in its appendix.

authority.label: Staff-domain meaning proposal; specialist review required

records.label: Guarantee Credit
records.scope: Frozen-source staff-question research. Source text is not current-law assurance and proposed meaning is not an official interpretation. Concept role: dwp:BenefitComponent.
records.text: The Guarantee Credit component of Pension Credit has a financial assessment and additional-amount dependencies distinct from Savings Credit.

authority.label: Existing authored research concept; specialist review required

records.label: Membership of the household
records.scope: Pension Credit source-discovery concept in the 15 September 2026 DMG snapshot. The entry point is not a complete legal definition; applicability, exceptions and current law require separate review.
records.text: Navigate to how membership of the household is addressed in the guide.

authority.label: Existing authored research concept; specialist review required

records.label: Housing costs
records.scope: Pension Credit source-discovery concept in the 15 September 2026 DMG snapshot. The entry point is not a complete legal definition; applicability, exceptions and current law require separate review.
records.text: Find the housing-cost section, subtopics and appendices; this record does not calculate housing costs.

authority.label: Existing authored research concept; specialist review required

records.label: Incapacity Benefit contribution-record referral
records.scope: This is not permission for the project to settle a contribution dispute. Late contributions, credited years, relevant benefit years, linking periods, revision and supersession remain separate legal questions within the legacy regime.
records.text: The captured IB guidance distinguishes the DM’s contribution-condition decision from an HMRC formal decision needed when the underlying national insurance contribution record is disputed.

authority.label: Existing authored research concept; specialist review required

records.label: Incapacity Benefit: the captured legacy claim boundary
records.scope: This is legacy guidance, not a new claim route for ESA or Universal Credit. The source retains contribution, incapacity and transitional provisions. The exception, chapter 45 and statutory versions need review before applying the date to any real claim.
records.text: The Incapacity Benefit introduction records its replacement of earlier sickness/invalidity benefits and a closure to claims from 31 January 2011, subject to the exception it signposts for certain existing disability-related Income Support claimants.

authority.label: Existing authored research concept; specialist review required

records.label: IB in youth: contribution and overlap classifications
records.scope: “Contributory” is purpose-specific here. Do not infer a contribution requirement from the overlap label or treat the label as an ontology-wide contradiction. Retained SDA, age, incapacity, residence and historical claim restrictions still matter.
records.text: The source describes IB(Y) as an IB category that is not based on contribution conditions, while expressly treating it as contributory for the purpose of overlapping-benefit rules.

authority.label: Existing authored research concept; specialist review required

records.label: IIDB assessment and waiting-period boundaries
records.scope: Neither a single percentage nor a universal 90-day wait describes every case. DMG 69013 names disease-specific exceptions and a distinction between date of onset and addition to the schedule. No assessment, onset date, rate or award is computed.
records.text: The source separates pre-1 October 1986 and later assessment conditions, including aggregation and disease-specific thresholds, and distinguishes onset and waiting-period exceptions.

authority.label: Existing authored research concept; specialist review required

records.label: IIDB injury, loss of faculty and disablement
records.scope: These are IIDB assessment concepts, not universal disability definitions or a finding about any person. Conditions differ before and from 1 October 1986, and accidents and prescribed diseases have exceptions. No percentage is assigned.
records.text: The source distinguishes injury, impaired bodily or mental function, disability and the aggregate disablement assessment, rather than using all four terms interchangeably.

authority.label: Existing authored research concept; specialist review required

records.label: Medical and non-medical questions in an IIDB decision
records.scope: A favourable accident decision does not itself settle all IIDB questions. The source calls for keeping papers together where one accident affects multiple benefits to avoid conflicting decisions. This project has no decision-making authority.
records.text: The IIDB chapter describes an outcome decision containing both medical questions, such as diagnosis and disablement, and non-medical questions, such as employment and rate.

authority.label: Staff-domain meaning proposal; specialist review required

records.label: Income other than earnings
records.scope: Frozen-source staff-question research. Source text is not current-law assurance and proposed meaning is not an official interpretation. Concept role: dwp:AssessmentInput.
records.text: Named income types and individual disregards must be read with their scopes; inclusion in a list alone does not determine an award.

authority.label: Existing authored research concept; specialist review required

records.label: Employment connection of an industrial accident
records.scope: An event on work premises is not automatically an industrial accident. Employed-earner status, treated groups, excluded groups, territorial scope and statutory extensions must be reviewed. This source-specific test is not the same as tort negligence or all self-employed work.
records.text: The source separates “arising out of” from “in the course of” employment and examines when, where and what the person was doing, with further enquiry sometimes needed even during normal work.

authority.label: Existing authored research concept; specialist review required

records.label: Industrial accident question and a benefit claim
records.scope: Read the full conditions in DMG 66001 and the qualification in 66002; the project does not decide whether an accident occurred. The “accident is the injury” case type has separate guidance in 69022. From 5 December 2012 the source restricts applications for declarations without an IA claim.
records.text: The chapter distinguishes an identifiable accident arising out of and in the course of employed-earner employment, with territorial limits, from the later personal-injury and benefit questions.

authority.label: Existing authored research concept; specialist review required

records.label: Industrial Injuries decisions and medical advice
records.scope: The date is a source-stated procedural transition, not the PDF publication date. Medical expertise informs the decision; it does not confer adjudication authority on a model. Complete current procedures and delegated responsibilities need verification.
records.text: The source describes a 5 July 1999 change to decisions made on behalf of the Secretary of State by lay decision makers, using all evidence including advice from doctors.

authority.label: Existing authored research concept; specialist review required

records.label: Compensation and damages in retained old-scheme guidance
records.scope: Read this within chapter 73’s expressly limited retained scope after 5 December 2012. The source distinguishes awards never received, other-disease compensation and before/after-claim damages. It is not a universal rule for modern IIDB, personal-injury compensation or bereavement payments.
records.text: The retained PB and MDB material distinguishes prior compensation entitlement from actual payment and distinguishes the timing effect of damages on weekly allowance from the timing effect on death benefit.

authority.label: Existing authored research concept; specialist review required

records.label: Death benefit in retained PB and MDB guidance
records.scope: This is not the BSP or general Bereavement Benefit regime and is not a newly opened claim route. All historical scheme, dependant and compensation conditions require legal review in the context of the 2012 abolition/transfer statement.
records.text: The retained old-scheme guidance describes a lump sum for specified dependants, with disease, death-date, pre-1948 employment and compensation conditions.

authority.label: Existing authored research concept; specialist review required

records.label: Old industrial schemes and the December 2012 transition
records.scope: The source retains limited guidance on compensation and death benefit and sends new claims for pre-5 July 1948 accidents/diseases to IIDB under its rules. This is not proof that every old-scheme paragraph still provides a current claim route.
records.text: The old-cases chapter describes ending the WC (Supplementation), PB and MDB schemes from 5 December 2012, transferring specified existing recipients and pending claims to IIDB.

authority.label: Existing authored research concept; specialist review required

records.label: Industrial Retirement Allowance and REA conversion
records.scope: This is Industrial Injuries Retirement Allowance, not State Pension or Retirement Pension. Historical examples using age 65 do not establish current pensionable age. The source’s rate and threshold figures are not applied as a calculation, and its post-1 October 1990 restriction on returning to REA remains explicit.
records.text: The industrial-injuries guidance distinguishes Retirement Allowance from REA, with conversion linked to pensionable age, regular employment and prior REA conditions, and separate award/payment days.

authority.label: Existing authored research concept; specialist review required

records.label: Industrial Injuries scheme components and boundaries
records.scope: The opening paragraph calls the scheme non-contributory but its next numbered phrase says “no fault contributory”; this internal wording inconsistency is retained as a source-owner question. Component introductions include closed routes and dated conditions, not a current menu of new claims.
records.text: The source lists IIDB, US, CAA, ESDA, REA, RA and retained old/death-benefit cases as different components, with IIDB linked to loss of faculty from an industrial accident or prescribed disease.

authority.label: Existing authored research concept; specialist review required

records.label: Evidence where an accident was unreported or unwitnessed
records.scope: No accident is assumed true or false from missing records alone. DMG 66046 continues onto the next page; the selected categories are not a complete evidential checklist. The project records evidence needs without collecting personal accident details.
records.text: The source says absence of an accident record does not itself defeat a claim, while delay, explanations, consistency, corroboration and medical evidence may require investigation.

authority.label: Existing authored research concept; specialist review required

records.label: Actual habitual residence in the cited benefit guidance
records.scope: DMG 072780 and 072791 concern the source-defined test and the CTA defined at 072786. No universal residence duration or equivalence with a qualifying right to reside is asserted.
records.text: The source describes habitual residence as a factual question to be considered from all the circumstances, and distinguishes domestic and EC-law considerations.

authority.label: Existing authored research concept; specialist review required

records.label: AA, DLA care and CA classification in the cited EU regime
records.scope: DMG 071752 concerns a specific coordination classification and cites judgments dated 18 October 2007 and 5 May 2011. Classification alone does not establish exportability; the subsequent export paragraph has personal-scope, competency and memo dependencies not resolved here.
records.text: For the cited EU coordination rules, the source classifies AA, the care component of DLA and CA as sickness benefits in cash for long-term care. It separates that classification from the DLA mobility component.

authority.label: Existing authored research concept; specialist review required

records.label: Residence for Category C and D Retirement Pension
records.scope: DMG 075760 and 075772 concern the named legacy pension categories and the cited Regulation 1408/71 provisions. They are not a statement of new State Pension or Pension Credit conditions.
records.text: The cited guidance distinguishes residence conditions for becoming entitled to Category C or D Retirement Pension from provisions retaining an existing entitlement in another EEA country.

authority.label: Existing authored research concept; specialist review required

records.label: Retention of Category C or D pension in another EEA country
records.scope: DMG 075772 preserves the initial-entitlement versus retention boundary. It neither creates a general pension export right nor resolves later legal changes.
records.text: The source explicitly says provisions retaining an existing Category C or D pension entitlement abroad do not themselves satisfy the residence conditions for first becoming entitled.

authority.label: Existing authored research concept; specialist review required

records.label: Territorial and transitional dates of coordination regulations
records.scope: DMG 071751 is a source-stated legal regime history: 1 May 2010, 1 April 2012 and 1 June 2012 have different territorial roles. Its word “current” is source wording, not a project claim of UK applicability in 2026. Post-transition instruments and individual scope remain unresolved.
records.text: The source distinguishes Regulations 883/2004 and 987/2009 from the earlier regulations and records different start dates for EU Member States, Switzerland and Norway, Iceland and Liechtenstein, with transitional cases retained.

authority.label: Existing authored research concept; specialist review required

records.label: DLA mobility classification and the stated export boundary
records.scope: DMG 071752 and 071800 must retain the component distinction and the 071743 transitional-protection dependency. Neither DLA components nor DLA and ESA are declared equivalent. This is not advice about a current claim.
records.text: The source identifies DLA mobility as a special non-contributory benefit and gives it a different export treatment from DLA care, with a reference to transitional protection.

authority.label: Existing authored research concept; specialist review required

records.label: Personal scope in the cited EC coordination regime
records.scope: DMG 070050 cites Regulations 1408/71 and 574/72 and Memo 32/10. This is the source-described legacy regime; no present UK or post-transition coverage is inferred. DMG 070311 is qualified by “in general” and refers onwards to 070320.
records.text: The cited guidance treats personal scope as a condition for coverage by the EC provisions and distinguishes that coverage from reliance on a reciprocal agreement.

authority.label: Existing authored research concept; specialist review required

records.label: EUSS pre-settled status and the source’s qualifying-right question
records.scope: DMG 073492 explicitly refers to Memos 01/21, 01-22 and 14/25. Their effect and later case law are unresolved here. This records a bounded source statement and must not be converted into a current categorical refusal rule. The same captured part then presents an AT destitution assessment at DMG 073496–073499 (Memo 15-25): PDF page 117 uses UC wording, while its continuation and Example 1 on page 118 concern SPC. This is an explicit unresolved qualification and cross-benefit wording issue within the acquired source, not a resolved legal mapping. The judgment, Withdrawal Agreement scope, dated exclusions and memo require reconciliation before any refusal inference.
records.text: The source identifies EUSS pre-settled status as limited leave and says it does not automatically establish the relevant qualifying right for the listed benefits.

authority.label: Existing authored research concept; specialist review required

records.label: EUSS settled status in the source-described residence test
records.scope: DMG 073490–073491; this concerns one element of the test, not complete benefit entitlement or a finding of actual habitual residence. The applicable benefit and later legal changes still require review.
records.text: The source identifies EUSS settled status as indefinite leave and says it satisfies the right-to-reside element of the stated habitual residence test.

authority.label: Existing authored research concept; specialist review required

records.label: The source-described habitual residence assessment sequence
records.scope: DMG 072791–072792 are scoped by the IS, income-based JSA, income-related ESA and SPC introduction at 072770. Memo 10/25 and other later references are unresolved. No sequence here determines a real claim.
records.text: The guidance separates immigration-control and exclusion questions, a qualifying right to reside, excluded rights, and the factual assessment of actual habitual residence.

authority.label: Existing authored research concept; specialist review required

records.label: Income-based JSA international residence scope
records.scope: DMG 075330 and the onward 075550 reference; the passage identifies a distinct question but does not establish its complete test, current availability or applicability to UC.
records.text: The source lists restrictions on income-based JSA for a person who has come from abroad separately from the contribution conditions supported by foreign insurance.

authority.label: Existing authored research concept; specialist review required

records.label: Industrial Injuries claims and export as separate questions
records.scope: DMG 074361 is a substantive scope statement, not sufficient evidence of export entitlement. Detailed conditions, treaty coverage and legal currency remain unresolved.
records.text: The Industrial Injuries section treats claims from outside Great Britain and export of an existing benefit as separate topics, each with domestic, EC or reciprocal-agreement provisions.

authority.label: Existing authored research concept; specialist review required

records.label: Industrial Injuries international residence and presence scope
records.scope: DMG 074360–074362 list Disablement Benefit, Reduced Earnings Allowance, Retirement Allowance and Industrial Death Benefit. The chapter directs other schemes elsewhere. No extension to ESA or to every industrial-injury payment is inferred.
records.text: The guidance covers named Industrial Injuries benefits and distinguishes domestic conditions, EC provisions and reciprocal agreements when considering residence and presence.

authority.label: Existing authored research concept; specialist review required

records.label: Type A invalidity legislation in the cited EC framework
records.scope: DMG 074080–074082 cite Regulation 1408/71 and concern invalidity benefit or long-term Incapacity Benefit. This is not a classification of current ESA or New Style ESA, nor an award calculation.
records.text: The cited framework distinguishes Type A legislation, where the invalidity-benefit rate does not depend on insurance length, from Type B legislation.

authority.label: Existing authored research concept; specialist review required

records.label: Type B invalidity legislation in the cited EC framework
records.scope: DMG 074080–074082; national legislation, insured periods and the applicable coordination regime remain separate dependencies. The association with Type A records a distinction, not equivalence.
records.text: The cited framework identifies Type B legislation by dependence of the invalidity-benefit rate on the length of insurance, in contrast with Type A legislation.

authority.label: Existing authored research concept; specialist review required

records.label: Foreign insurance in the source’s contribution-based JSA scope
records.scope: DMG 075330–075331 retain the older JSA terminology and the distinction between UK JSA and the broader abbreviation UB. The page bears an amendment label of June 2007; this is not a New Style JSA rule.
records.text: The source distinguishes using insurance from another country for contribution-based JSA from the residence restrictions attached to income-based JSA.

authority.label: Existing authored research concept; specialist review required

records.label: Mariner definition for Industrial Injuries in the source
records.scope: DMG 078070 is deliberately separate from the other-benefits definition at 078071. The statutory versions and the special forces exclusion at 078072 remain relevant; the definitions are not equated.
records.text: For Industrial Injuries benefits, the source’s mariner definition requires the specified shipboard contract-of-service employment to be treated as employed earner’s employment.

authority.label: Existing authored research concept; specialist review required

records.label: Mariner definition for other benefits in the source
records.scope: DMG 078071–078072 use historical source wording and have a forces exception. It is not sufficient to identify anyone working on a vessel as a mariner for every benefit.
records.text: The other-benefits definition describes shipboard roles and gives further connection and UK-contract conditions for employment in another capacity on board.

authority.label: Existing authored research concept; specialist review required

records.label: Presence for the stated GB and Northern Ireland arrangements
records.scope: This is the procedural meaning used in DMG 070531–070532, subject to the benefit exclusions in 070533. It is not equated with habitual residence, ordinary residence or international benefit export.
records.text: For the stated cross-border revision, supersession or appeal arrangements, the guidance distinguishes being “in” the other country from casual presence and otherwise retains the original decision country.

authority.label: Existing authored research concept; specialist review required

records.label: Benefit scope of the stated GB and Northern Ireland review arrangements
records.scope: DMG 070530–070533, including Memo 1/17, are read together. The general statement in 070530 is not applied universally. The agreement text, amendments and current jurisdiction remain unverified.
records.text: The source describes cross-border revision, supersession and appeal arrangements, then excludes named benefits including Pension Credit and UC from reviews or appeals under that agreement.

authority.label: Existing authored research concept; specialist review required

records.label: Continental shelf area distinctions in the source
records.scope: DMG 078082–078084 require the relevant statutory definition and purpose. These historical territorial descriptions do not identify a present boundary or establish benefit jurisdiction for a location.
records.text: The source distinguishes a UK designated area from a prescribed area involving Norway or other EC countries outside their territorial waters, and warns that accidents and diseases use different definitions.

authority.label: Existing authored research concept; specialist review required

records.label: Continental shelf prescribed employment in the source
records.scope: DMG 078080–078081 are qualified by the separate accident and disease definitions at 078084. No ordinary land-based employment or whole-UK territorial rule is substituted.
records.text: The source describes a continental shelf worker by prescribed employment and says the relevant employment can be under a contract of service or otherwise in an appointed or designated area.

authority.label: Existing authored research concept; specialist review required

records.label: Source-described delayed claims caused by specified overseas employment
records.scope: DMG 078100 is conditional on both the employment-related impediment and prompt subsequent action. It is not an unlimited overseas deadline extension or a rule for every claimant abroad.

records.label: SPC claimant temporary absence in the source
records.scope: Frozen-source staff-question research. Source text is not current-law assurance and proposed meaning is not an official interpretation. Concept role: dwp:DecisionRule.
records.text: Source-bounded Pension Credit research through DMG 077001–077004, not a rule for all benefits. Other entitlement conditions must continue. The captured four-week branch requires an absence not expected to exceed four weeks; the examples distinguish expected duration from an early return or later extension. The eight-week branch requires the specified death connection, an absence not expected to exceed eight weeks and the Secretary of State considering return within four weeks unreasonable. The twenty-six-week branch requires an absence not expected to exceed twenty-six weeks and solely for the specified treatment, medically approved convalescence or care, or accompanying the specified person. Preserve the practitioner, pre-existing-condition and accompanying-person qualifications exactly as stated on pages 9–11; being abroad when an accident occurs is not itself the stated purpose condition. The qualified-practitioner definition continues onto page 11. Household membership, qualifying young person, the dated 2016 transition and the source-described non-export boundary need separate conditional review. Destination, purpose, expected and actual duration, relevant date and household facts remain unknown. Statutory reconciliation and the DMG 04642 supersession cross-reference remain open.

authority.label: Existing authored research concept; specialist review required

records.label: Accommodation and a fixed address in JSA(IB) and IS

Current rates, transitional eligibility and children’s provisions are unresolved.
records.text: The captured guidance describes applicable amounts for JSA(IB) and IS through personal allowances and, where appropriate, additional components such as premiums, certain housing costs and transitional elements.

authority.label: Existing authored research concept; specialist review required

records.label: Beneficial and legal capital ownership in JSA(IB) and IS
records.scope: An account name alone does not resolve beneficial ownership. Joint interests, trusts, evidence presumptions and particular assets need separate examination. records.text: The captured capital chapter distinguishes a beneficial interest from holding capital in one’s name and explains that a legal owner may hold capital on trust for another beneficial owner.

authority.label: Existing authored research concept; specialist review required

records.label: Conditions for self-employed business expenses
records.scope: An entry in business accounts is not proof that the whole amount is deductible. The separate allowable and excluded categories, evidence and circumstances need review. This is a JSA/IS source model, not tax advice or an assertion that HMRC and benefit expense rules are identical.
records.text: The captured passage conditions deduction of a business expense on business purpose, payment during the assessment period, reasonableness and allowability; mixed private and business use requires apportionment.

authority.label: Existing authored research concept; specialist review required

records.label: Purpose and ownership in deprivation of capital
records.scope: Spending or a gift alone does not establish deprivation for benefit purposes. The source distinguishes the JSA and IS wording, personal-injury trusts, diminishing notional capital, children and young people, capacity, enforceable debts and necessities. All facts and current legal applicability require review; no fraud or entitlement decision is made.
records.text: The captured chapter links notional capital after deprivation to a benefit purpose, prior beneficial ownership and the claimant or partner; it requires the decision maker to establish a significant purpose for each act.

authority.label: Existing authored research concept; specialist review required

records.label: Assessing a capital disregard for JSA(IB) and IS
records.scope: Each disregard has its own conditions and period; no blanket duration or current capital threshold is inferred. DMG 29351 carries a memo 11/20 call-out. The procedure resembles other chapters but does not establish equivalence with Pension Credit, and its source wording is not a specialist-approved rule.
records.text: The captured chapter requires evidence for a capital disregard, places the disregard question before valuation and says all applicable disregards for an item must be considered because they can affect income treatment.

authority.label: Existing authored research concept; specialist review required

records.label: Employed earner in the JSA and Income Support guidance
records.scope: The source expressly includes some office holders and points to legislation; this is not a universal employment-law or tax-status determination. records.text: The captured chapter describes an employed earner through gainful employment in Great Britain under a contract of service or in an office with general earnings.

authority.label: Existing authored research concept; specialist review required

records.label: Family income attribution for JSA(IB) and Income Support
records.scope: Do not apply this as a current rule for all children or all households. DMG 25007 carries a JSA/IS 64 memo call-out and a child-income cross-reference. JSA(Cont) is explicitly treated differently; polygamous-family provisions, chapter 30, transitional circumstances and current legal effects remain dependencies.
records.text: The captured chapter describes calculating and attributing income of specified family members for JSA(IB) or IS, while distinguishing joint claims and special rules involving an under-18 partner.

authority.label: Existing authored research concept; specialist review required

records.label: Free in-patient treatment in the JSA and IS guidance
records.scope: A hospital address or an NHS label alone is insufficient. Private-patient exceptions and the factual meaning of in-patient must be checked. records.text: The captured guidance requires several conditions together for free in-patient treatment: free maintenance, medical or other treatment, a hospital or similar institution, in-patient status and a specified legislative or Defence Council basis.

authority.label: Existing authored research concept; specialist review required

records.label: Gross employed earnings for JSA and Income Support

records.text: The source describes gross earnings after qualifying employment expenses and before authorised employer deductions, with a specific qualification for recovery of overpaid wages.

authority.label: Existing authored research concept; specialist review required

records.label: Gross income other than earnings for JSA(IB) and IS

records.text: For income other than earnings, the captured chapter starts with a gross amount and identifies specified sums and disregards to consider, rather than permitting all expenses or deductions.

authority.label: Existing authored research concept; specialist review required

records.label: Family membership during hospital admission
records.scope: The listed contexts include a lone parent, a couple, a polygamous marriage and a child or young person. The continuation of DMG 24097 is on PDF page 26; chapter 22 and any current benefit-specific consequences require separate examination.
records.text: The captured hospital guidance asks whether a patient remains a member of the family and routes that question to the separate family-membership chapter.

authority.label: Existing authored research concept; specialist review required

records.text: The captured general-income guidance requires the claim date, benefit-week start, due date, date treated as paid and the relevant payment period or prescribed alternative before determining the period of assessment.

authority.label: Existing authored research concept; specialist review required

records.scope: Frozen ADM adm-chapter-a4; captured role: substantive. Boundary: machine candidate, unresolved. A structural unit is not a complete legal rule or applicability decision. Capture dates are not effective dates. Check governing headings, definitions, exceptions and current source.
records.text:
Change notified outside the time limits

A4352 Where an advantageous change of circumstances is notified later than one month after it
occurred, or for UC after the end of the assessment period in which the change occurred (or such longer
period as the DM may have allowed under A4310 - A4315) then the effective date of the supersession
will be


1. for ESA and JSA1, from the beginning of the benefit week in which the notification was made


2. for PIP2, from the date of notification of the change (but see A4353)


3. for UC3, from the first day of the AP in which the notification was made (but see A4360 - A4361)


      1 UC, PIP, JSA & ESA (D&A) Regs Sch 1, part 1, para 6; 2 Sch 1, part 2, para 14; 3 Sch 1, part 3, para 21

records.label: Chapter A4: Supersession, suspension and termination — A4361 — UC
records.scope: Frozen ADM adm-chapter-a4; captured role: substantive. Boundary: machine candidate, unresolved. A structural unit is not a complete legal rule or applicability decision. Capture dates are not effective dates. Check governing headings, definitions, exceptions and current source.
records.text:
UC and award of other benefits

A4361 In the case of UC where the claimant or a member of their family becomes entitled to another
relevant benefit, ceases to be entitled or the rate of another such benefit alters then the superseding

decision takes effect1 from the first day of the assessment period in which entitlement to the other
benefit or an alteration in its rate arises or entitlement ends.


 1 SS Act 98, s 8(3); DAWAP(S)Regs, reg 2; DACYP (S)Regs, reg 2; UC, PIP, JSA & ESA (D&A) Regs, Sch 1,
                                                                                 Part 4, para 31(1) & 31(2)(a)


Example 1


Sam has been in receipt of UC from 21.11.19. On 28.5.20 she was awarded CA from 30.3.20 meaning that
she is also entitled to the carer element in UC. Sam didn't notify the change until 24.9.20. The
supersession effective date rule means that she did not have to report the change within a certain
period. The UC award is superseded on the grounds of a relevant change of circumstances and the carer
element is awarded from 21.3.20.


Example 2


Connor has been in receipt of UC from 14.12.18. On 11.5.21 his daughter was awarded DLA at the middle
rate from 8.2.21. He didn't notify the change until 26.5.21. The DM is satisfied that Connor had regular
and substantial caring responsibilities for a severely disabled person since 8.2.21 and so there is a clear
and direct link between the award of DLA and entitlement to the carer element. The supersession
effective date rule means that he did not have to report the change within a certain period. The UC award
is superseded on the grounds of a relevant change of circumstances and the carer element is awarded
from 14.1.21.


Example 3


Matt is in receipt of UC and JSA. He starts part time work and receives payment from this employment in
the final week of his assessment period. His award of JSA is terminated. The DM supersedes the award

of UC from the first day of the assessment period so that JSA is no longer taken into account when
determining the amount of UC payable.

records.label: Chapter C1: Universal Credit: International issues — UC six-month medical-absence condition and examples
records.scope: Frozen ADM adm-chapter-c1; captured role: substantive. Boundary: agent-reviewed excerpt only. A structural unit is not a complete legal rule or applicability decision. Capture dates are not effective dates. Check governing headings, definitions, exceptions and current source.
records.text:
Six Months - Medical treatment

C1988 [See Memo ADM 09-25] In deciding whether a claimant satisfies the basic condition that they be
“in GB”, a temporary absence which is not expected to exceed and does not exceed 6 months is
disregarded where the absence was solely in connection with


1. the claimant undergoing1


      1.1 treatment for an illness or physical or mental impairment by, or under the supervision of, a
      qualified practitioner or


      1.2 medically approved (see note below) convalescence or care as a result of treatment for an
      illness or physical or mental impairment, provided that the claimant had that illness or disability
      before leaving GB or


2. the claimant accompanying their partner, or a child or QYP for whom they are responsible where that

partner, child or QYP is undergoing2


      2.1 treatment for an illness or physical or mental impairment by or under the supervision of a
      qualified practitioner or


      2.2 medically approved (see note below) convalescence or care as a result of treatment for an
      illness or physical or mental impairment provided the partner, child or QYP had that illness or
      disability before leaving GB.


      Note: “medically approved” means3 certified by a medical practitioner


                                                            1 UC Regs, reg 11(3)(a); 2 reg 11(3)(b); 3 reg 11(5)


Example 1


Joseph suffers from severe depression he goes to France for some specific therapy. This lasts for a total
of four months. The trip was solely in connection with a mental impairment and given by a qualified
medical practitioner. The DM decides that the claimant is temporarily absent for four months and
remains entitled to UC throughout.


Example 2

Paul a UC claimant who travelled to Cyprus on holiday on 1 August 2021 with the intention of staying for
3 weeks. Unfortunately, whilst on holiday he had an accident and needed a hip replacement which meant
he could not travel for 8 weeks. As a result, Paul was outside the UK for more than one month. The
accident occurred after Paul had left GB. The DM determined the claimant was not entitled to UC from 2
September 2021 when Paul’s absence exceeded one month.


Example 3


Jack and Jill have saved up for their dream holiday in Australia. They leave the UK on 01/05/21 and have a
return flight booked for 31/05/21. On arrival in Australia, while entering the airport, the sign above the
main building falls from its mounting, breaking Jack’s back and leaving him immobile and in a coma. On
02/06/21 Jill informs DWP that they will be unable to leave Australia for at least six months as she is
needed at his bedside to try to bring him out of the coma, and will then need to help Jack’s long medical
recuperation before he is able to board a flight home. The DM decides that the disregard of the absence
cannot be extended to six months under Reg 11(3) of the Universal Credit Regulations 2013 because
they did not go abroad for the sole purpose of receiving medical treatment for the accident that was to
befall them in Australia. Jack and Jill are not entitled to UC from 2 June 2021 until they return to GB.

Meaning of “partner”
C1990 A partner means1 the other member of a couple “couple” is defined in the Act 2 as meaning


1. a man and woman who are married to each other and are members of the same household;


2. a man and woman who are not married to each other but are living together as husband and wife;

as if they were civil partners if, and only if, they would be treated as living together as husband and wife
were they of opposite sexes.

records.text:
Definitions E2090 - E2099



Child E2090 - E2091


Qualifying young person E2092 - E2099




Child

E2090 Child means1 a person under the age of 16.


Note: There is no need for the child to be receiving education for this definition to apply.


                                                                                           1 WR Act 12, s 40


E2091



Qualifying young person

E2092 A qualifying young person is a person who has reached the age of 16 but not the age of 20 and
who is


1. aged 16 years, but only for the period up to, but not including, the 1st September that next follows their
16th birthday


2. aged 19 years, but only for the period up to, but not including, the 1st September that next follows their
19th birthday where they are enrolled on, or accepted for


      2.1 approved training1 or


      2.2 a course of education


      this must not include meal breaks or unsupervised study, including homework, whether done on or

      off the premises of the educational establishment 2.


            2.2.a which is not advanced education


            2.2.b at a school, college or other establishment that is approved by the Secretary of State


            2.2.c where they spend on average more than twelve hours a week during term time in

             receiving tuition doing examinations or practical work or supervised study


3. aged 19 and has been


      3.1 undertaking a course of education or training or


      3.2 accepted or enrolled for a course of education or training


      before reaching that age3


Note 1: The education or training described in 3.1 and 3.2 does not include education or training that is

provided through a contract of employment4.


Note 2: A person shall be treated as undertaking a course of FTE during the period between the end of
one course and the start of another where the person is accepted for or enrolled on the latter course.


Note 3: Where a child or qualifying young person turns 16 or 19 on the 31st August the period described
at 1. and 2. will end on that same day.


                                                        1 UC Regs, reg 5(4); 2 reg 5(1); 3 reg 5(2); 4 reg 5(3)


E2093 Any person who falls within E2092 is not a qualifying young person if they are receiving UC, JSA

or ESA1. For example, twins both 18 and in education, one has a child and gets UC under 8(1)(d) and is
therefore not a qualifying young person the other twin is a qualifying young person.


                                                                                          1 UC Regs, reg 5(5)


Approved training
E2094 Approved training means training arranged under prescribed legislation 1 and approved by the
Secretary of State, and includes


1. Entry to Employment or Programme-Led Pathways


2. In Wales, Skillbuild, Skillbuild + or Foundation Modern Apprenticeships


3. In Scotland, Skillseekers, Get ready for work or Modern Apprenticeships.


       1 Employment and Training Act 1973, s 2(1); Enterprise and New Towns (Scotland) Act 1990, s 2(3)


Non-advanced education
E2095 Non-advanced education means any course of study which is of a standard up to, and including


1. advanced GNVQ (or equivalent)


2. A – levels (or equivalent)

3. Scottish national qualification (higher or advanced higher)


Note: These include, for example, the International Baccalaureate, National Diploma and Study
Programme in England

Introduction P1001 - P1010



P1001 [See ADM memo 11-25] PIP was introduced for new claimants from 8.4.131 in certain areas only
(see ADM Chapter P5 Appendix 1 for the postcodes affected). It was introduced in all other areas for new

claimants only from 10.6.132. For existing DLA claimants PIP was introduced after 27.10.13, but only
where a relevant date has been specified. It replaces DLA for working age claimants. PIP is an extra
costs benefit for people who have a limited or severely limited ability to carry out daily living or mobility
activities.


Note: See ADM Chapter P5 for the definition of relevant date and for guidance on transitional provisions.


         1 WR Act 12 Commencement Order No. 8, Art 8; 2 WR Act 12 Commencement Order No.10, Art 2

records.scope: Frozen ADM adm-chapter-p4; captured role: substantive. Boundary: agent-reviewed excerpt only. A structural unit is not a complete legal rule or applicability decision. Capture dates are not effective dates. Check governing headings, definitions, exceptions and current source.
records.text:
New claims and entitlement to PIP when reaching the relevant age
P4076-P4086



Meaning of relevant age P4076-P4079


Further claims when claimant has reached the relevant age P4080-P4084


Claims following an award of ADP where claimant has reached the relevant age P4085- P4086



Meaning of relevant age

P4076 The relevant age means


1. age 65 or


2. if higher pensionable age1.


                                                     1 WR Act 12, s 83(1); Pensions Act 19 95, Sch 4, para 1


P4077 A claimant will continue to be entitled to PIP if they are entitled to an award of


1. the daily living component or


2. the mobility component or


3. both


on the day preceding the day on which they reached the relevant age.


                                                                                  1 SS (PIP) Regs, reg 25(a)


P4078 A claimant is entitled to PIP if


1. they make a claim for PIP before reaching the relevant age and


2. although that claim is not determined before they reached the relevant age 1 an award of


is subsequently made in respect of them.


      2.1 the daily living component or


      2.2 the mobility component or


      2.3 both

                                                                                        1 SS (PIP) Regs, reg 25(b)


P4079 Rules for those claimants approaching the age of 16 are dealt with in ADM Chapter P5.



Further claims when claimant has reached the relevant age

General
P4080 [See memo ADM 6/25] Where the previous award is in respect of only the daily living

component1 then the DM cannot additionally award any rate of the mobility component on a further
claim.


                                                                                     1 SS (PIP) Regs, reg 15 & 26


P4081 Where a decision is made on entitlement on the further claim and the conditions are substantially

the same mental or physical condition, the required period condition 1 is amended to the effect that the
claimant does not need to satisfy the 3 month qualifying period (see ADM Chapter P1 for required period

condition)2.


                                                           1 SS (PIP) Regs, reg 15(2) and (3); 2 reg 12, 13 and 14


12 month linking rule
P4082 If the claimant makes a new claim for PIP


1. after the age of 651 and


2. within 12 months of the previous award ending2 and


3. was previously entitled to an award of PIP for


         3.1 substantially the same condition or conditions for which the previous award was made 3 or


         3.2 a new condition which developed as a result of a condition for which the previous award was

         made4


a new award for the same component5 at the same rate of PIP can be made6.


    1 SS (PIP) Regs, reg 26(2)(a); 2 reg 26(2)(b); 3 reg 15(1)d)(i); 4 reg 15(1)(d)(ii); 5 reg 15(1)(c) 6 reg 26(2) &
                                                                                                               15(2)


Example


Sharon, who was aged 64, had been in receipt of PIP at the standard rate for both the daily living and the
mobility component for 12 months following a stroke. She had then improved and been reassessed and

the PIP entitlement was removed. 9 months after PIP ceased, but after reaching the age of 65, Sharon
had a further stroke. The condition was the same as before but her needs had increased, and as the
period between claims was less than 12 months, she did not have to serve the QP again for the standard
rate of either component to be paid. After the QP had been served for the enhanced rate the daily living
component would be increased. Although her needs were substantially worse, she could only receive the
standard rate of the mobility component due to the PIP rules (see P4083 for mobility component rules).


Mobility component
P4083 When the claimant makes a further claim and entitlement on that claim and the previous award
result from substantially the same conditions in P4080 3.1 or 3.2 then the DM can only make an award
of


1. the enhanced rate if the claimant was entitled to that rate on the previous award 1 or


2. the standard rate2 equal to the previous award or at a lower rate if they no longer satisfy the
conditions for the enhanced rate.


The new award cannot be greater than the previous award even if the conditions for that rate are met. 3


                                     1 SS (PIP) Regs, reg 26(2)(c)(i); 2 reg 26(2)(c)(ii) and (d); 3 reg 26(2)(c)(ii)


Daily living component
P4084 Where the DM makes an award of the mobility component under P4083, then an award of the
daily living component may additionally be made irrespective of whether the claimant had previously had

an award for daily living component1.


                                                                               1 SS (PIP) Regs, reg 15(2) &26(2)


Example


Richard’s date of birth is 21.6.49 and he was awarded DLA and then re-assessed and awarded PIP until
17.8.14. His PIP award was for enhanced rate mobility only. His award then stops and he fails to make a
new claim, as he is taken ill and in hospital from July 2014 until September 2014 and then recuperating at
home. On 15.2.15 Richard claims PIP again. This is within 12 months of his previous award ceasing. His
condition has deteriorated with the same disability as before. He is assessed by the DM as being entitled
to the enhanced rate of mobility component and the standard rate of daily living component. He is
subsequently paid PIP at these rates due to the linking provision, from the date of his new claim. This is
because he has claimed within 1 year of his previous claim, his required period condition is satisfied for
the mobility component and his daily living component is satisfied as it is more than 6 months since his
hospitalisation and deterioration.

Claims following an award of ADP where claimant has reached the relevant
age

P4085 Where a claimant who was previously in receipt of an ADP award:


1. makes a new PIP claim after reaching the relevant age; and


2. that previous award of ADP ended no more than 1 year before the date on which the new PIP claim is

made1; and


3. the previous ADP award was the same component as the one the claimant is entitled to under the new
PIP claim; and


4. the DM determines that entitlement for the new claim results from:


4.1. substantially the same mental or physical condition or conditions for which the previous ADP award
was made; or


4.2. a new condition which developed as a result of a condition for which the previous ADP award was
made


then the prescribed date for the 3-month part of the required period condition is the end of the previous
ADP award, and the 9-month part is the date the new PIP claim is made. This means that the 3-month
part will be considered in relation to the previous ADP award and does not need to be re-satisfied for the
new PIP claim.


                                                                              1 SS (PIP) Regs 2013, reg 26




P4086 When the new PIP claim is made, and the Decision Maker determines that entitlement on that
claim and the previous ADP award arises from substantially the same conditions in P4085 4.1 or 4.2,

then they can only make an award of the mobility component at1


1. the enhanced rate if the claimant was entitled to that rate for the previous ADP award; or


2. the standard rate equal to the previous ADP award, or at a lower rate if they no longer satisfy the
conditions for the enhanced rate.


                                                                              1. SS (PIP) Regs 2013, reg 26

Definitions P5004 - P5014




Assessment determination
P5004 Assessment determination1 means the determination following the assessment of the person’s
ability to carry out activities.


                                                                                    1 PIP (TP) Regs, reg 2(1)


Change of circumstances
P5005 Change of circumstances means a change of circumstances which a person might reasonably
have been expected to know might affect the continuance of that person’s entitlement to DLA, (by
ending entitlement to one or both components or resulting in entitlement to one or both components at

a different rate)1.


                                                                                   1 PIP (TP) Regs, reg 2(1).


DLA entitled person
P5006 A DLA entitled person1 means a person aged 16 or over who is entitled to either or both
components of DLA.


                                                                                    1 PIP (TP) Regs, reg 2(1)


Electronic communication
P5007 Has the meaning given by the legislation relating to electronic communications 1.


                                              1 PIP (TP) Regs, reg 2(1); UC, PIP, JSA, ESA(C&P) Regs, Sch 2


Notified person
P5008 A notified person1 means a DLA entitled person who has been sent a notification by the
Secretary of State to invite them to claim PIP.


                                                                                    1 PIP (TP) Regs, reg 2(1)


Relevant date
P5009 The relevant date is the date


1. which is specified by the Secretary of State in relation to a DLA entitled person and

2. from which the Secretary of State is satisfied that satisfactory arrangements will be in place to assess

entitlement of a DLA entitled person to PIP 1.


                                                                                    1 PIP (TP) Regs, reg 2(1)


P5010 As soon as practicable after specifying a relevant date, the Secretary of State must publish
sufficient information to enable a DLA entitled person to ascertain the relevant date, if any, which applies
to them. The information will be published in such manner as the Secretary of State considers

appropriate1 (see Appendix 2 to this Chapter for identified areas).


                                                                                   1 PIP (TP) Regs, reg 2(4)


Transfer claimant
P5011 Transfer claimant means a


1. notified person who has claimed PIP in response to a notification sent by the Secretary of State 1 or


2. voluntary transfer claimant.


                                                                                    1 PIP (TP) Regs, reg 2(1)


Voluntary transfer claimant
P5012 Voluntary transfer claimant1 means a DLA entitled person who has not received a notification but
who claims PIP.


                                                                                    1 PIP (TP) Regs, reg 2(1)

Determination of claim for PIP made

P5062 When an assessment determination is made by the DM on a claim by a transfer claimant


1. the DM will, as soon as is practicable, send the claimant written notification of the outcome decision
and


2. DLA will be terminated, on the last day of the period of 28 days starting with the first pay day after the

making of the determination1.


                                                                                     1 PIP (TP) Regs, reg 17(1)


P5063 When the outcome decision is an award of either or both PIP components, the claimant’s
entitlement to PIP will begin


1. from the day immediately following the day the claimant’s entitlement to DLA terminates 1 or


2. immediately following the last day of the period of 28 days as calculated in P5035 starting with the
first pay day after making the determination.


                                                                                     1 PIP (TP) Regs, reg 17(2)


P5064 The notifications issued must contain the information1 if


1. PIP is awarded, the day on which

      1.1 the claimant’s entitlement to DLA will terminate and


      1.2 the claimant’s entitlement to PIP will start


2. DLA is not awardedand a claim for PIP was made after the refusal 2


      2.1 where PIP is awarded, DLA will terminate on the day before the day the claimant becomes
      entitled to PIP or


      2.2 where PIP is not awarded, DLA will terminate on the first pay day following the period of 28

      days after the PIP assessment decision is made3.


                                                               1 PIP (TP) Regs, reg 17(3); 2 reg 17(4); 3 reg 17(5)

records.text:
Extension of fixed term period awards of DLA

For under 16s
P5066 Where there is an award of DLA for a DLA entitled person


1. and the award is of


      1.1 both components and in respect of either or both components is for a FTP or


      1.2 one component only and for a FTP and


2. the person reaches age 16 after 27.10.13 and


3. the FTP expires in the period starting with the day before the person reaches 16, and ending with the
date before the person reaches age 16 years and 6 months


the DM will extend the FTP1.


                                                                                   1 PIP (TP) Regs, reg 18(1)


P5067 Any such extended FTP will expire, and entitlement to DLA will terminate, on the day before the

claimant reaches 171, unless

1. entitlement to DLA ceases before that date or


2. a negative determination is made, then an earlier date will apply or


3. there is a failure to supply information and a negative determination is made.


                                                                                    1 PIP (TP) Regs, reg 18(2)


For working age claimants
P5068 When


1. an award of DLA to a claimant is for a FTP in regards to one or both components and


2. they are over the age of 16 and


3. the DM considers the FTP may expire before an assessment determination can be made


the DM can extend the period by such further period as the DM considers appropriate 1.


                                                                                    1 PIP (TP) Regs, reg 19(1)


P5069 The DM can extend1 a FTP


1. regardless of whether the person has yet made a claim for PIP and


2. where the FTP has already been extended and


3. on more than one occasion.


                                                                                    1 PIP (TP) Regs, reg 19(2)


P5070 An extended FTP will expire


1. on the last day of the period by which the DM extended or last extended it 1or


2. where the person’s entitlement to DLA terminates on an earlier day, on that day.


                                                                                    1 PIP (TP) Regs, reg 19(3)

records.scope: Frozen ADM adm-chapter-p5; captured role: transitional. Boundary: agent-reviewed excerpt only. A structural unit is not a complete legal rule or applicability decision. Capture dates are not effective dates. Check governing headings, definitions, exceptions and current source.
records.text:
Invitations to DLA claimants to claim PIP
P5016 Any time after 27.10.13 the Secretary of State may invite by written notification a DLA entitled

person, whose only or principle residence is located in an identified area to make a claim for PIP 1 (see
Appendix 2 to this Chapter).


                                                                                    1 PIP (TP) Regs, reg 3(1)


P5017 The Secretary of State shall not send a notification to any person who was aged 65 or over on

8.4.131.


                                                                                    1 PIP (TP) Regs, reg 3(2)


P5018 The Secretary of State will send an invitation to claim PIP to a DLA entitled person who reaches

the age of 16 after 27.10.13, or as soon as reasonably practicable after the person reaches that age 1.


                                                                                     1 PIP (TP) Reg, reg 3(3)


P5019 However, P5018 will only apply where


1. the Secretary of State has specified a relevant date which applies to the DLA entitled person and


2. the DLA entitled person reaches age 16 on or after the relevant date 1.


                                                                                  1 PIP (TP) Regs, reg 3(3A)


P5020 P5018 does not apply where, on the day they reach the age of 16, the person is entitled to DLA

on the basis of being terminally ill1 within the meaning of ADM P2077.


                                                                                    1 PIP (TP) Regs, reg 3(4)

P5021 P5018 also does not apply where the DLA entitled person entered hospital or a similar institution
as an in-patient under the age of 18. If this is the case they should not be invited to claim PIP until they
are discharged1. This will be the case even if the claimant reports a change of circumstance whilst in
hospital.2 If the claimant’s DLA is due to expire whilst they are still an in-patient in the hospital or similar
institution, the DLA award may be extended appropriately3 if the claimant continues to satisfy the
conditions of entitlement.


                                                   1 PIP (TP) Regs, reg 2(1) & 3(4A); 2 reg 3(5B); 3 reg 19(1)(b)


Example


Katy is aged 15 and is due to turn 16 on 19.7.16. She is entitled to the highest rate of the care component
and the higher rate of the mobility component of DLA from 21.6.14 – 20.6.17. She enters hospital on
18.7.16 and remains there as an in-patient until 23.8.18. Her DLA will not be stopped for any period as she
was under the age of 18 on the day she entered the hospital as an in-patient. As Katy’s DLA is due to
expire on 20.6.17 it will be extended as appropriate whilst she is in hospital. She will not be invited to
claim PIP until she is discharged.


Example 2


Declan is entitled to the highest rate of the care component and the higher rate of the mobility
component of DLA. He turns 16 on 17.9.16 and is invited to claim PIP. On 30.9.16 Declan makes a claim to
PIP. He is subsequently taken into hospital on 5.10.16. Although he is now a hospital in-patient, Declan’s
PIP claim continues. A decision is made on his PIP claim that his DLA will terminate on 23.11.16 and he
will be entitled to the enhanced rate of the daily living component and the enhanced rate of the mobility
component of PIP from 24.11.16 – 23.11.19. He is paid DLA up to 23.11.16 and payment of PIP from
24.11.16 will continue whilst he remains in hospital as he was under the age of 18 when he was admitted
to hospital on 5.10.16 (see ADM Chapter P3 for PIP hospitalisation rules).


P5022 When a DLA entitled claimant, who after 27.10.13, has neither


1. been sent an invitation to claim PIP 1nor


2. made a claim for PIP2


sends in a change of circumstances notification3, the Secretary of State will send the claimant an
invitation to claim PIP as soon as reasonably practicable (see P5035 and P5071).


Note 1: This does not include those persons who inform the DM that they are to be absent or have

become absent from GB, whether on a temporary or permanent basis 4.


Note 2: This does not apply where ADM P5021 applies.


                                                         1 PIP (TP) Reg, reg 3(1); 2 reg 4; 3 reg 3(5); 4 reg 3(6)

P5023 However, P5022 will only apply where


1. the Secretary of State has specified a relevant date which applies to that DLA entitled person and


2. the DLA entitled person reports the change of circumstances on or after the relevant date 1.


Note: If the DLA entitled person has not been given a relevant date, then the change of circumstances
should be taken into account for any DLA supersession action required.


                                                                                1 PIP (TP) Regs, reg 3(5A)
